task.name: mobile server 503
task.prompt: After ZP-68/69 the task server starts (Tailscale prompts for elevation) but opening the Funnel URL returns "HTTP error 503 Service Unavailable". Repro: Server menu -> Start Mobile Server, approve the Tailscale UAC prompt, open the https://*.ts.net URL on a phone or browser. Expected: the task page loads. Actual: 503. Likely cause: HttpListener is bound to http://localhost:{port}/ only, so a request that Tailscale Funnel forwards with Host: <node>.<tailnet>.ts.net matches no prefix and HttpListener answers 503. (The first request can also 503 briefly while Tailscale provisions the HTTPS cert.)
task.requirements: the Tailscale Funnel URL serves the task page (no 503); localhost still works; at most one extra UAC prompt
task.notes: Root cause confirmed: HttpListener answers 503 to any request whose Host/port matches none of its registered prefixes, and Tailscale Funnel forwards requests with the public Host (<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net) - which the localhost-only bind from ZP-68 never matched. Fix: in funnel mode StartListener now binds the wildcard http://+:{port}/ (accepts any Host); if Windows has no URL reservation it adds one elevated via `netsh http add urlacl` (a single UAC prompt - and Tailscale already elevates once anyway), then retries. If that is declined/fails it falls back to localhost + 127.0.0.1 and prints the exact netsh line plus a warning that the Funnel URL will 503 until it is run. Non-funnel mode (--no-funnel) stays localhost-only, no prompt. Also: after the funnel starts, SelfCheck() does a local GET and logs the status code so a backend problem is distinguishable from a Tailscale one, and the banner now notes the first request can 503 for ~10-30s while Tailscale provisions the HTTPS cert. Verified --no-funnel localhost serve still works and builds clean.

task.notes: Single-instance enforcement added. App.OnStartup takes a named Mutex ("zProject.SingleInstance.{GUID}"); if it is not the first instance it opens the named EventWaitHandle "zProject.Activate.{GUID}", Set()s it, and Shutdown()s before any window is created - so a second launch never runs. task.notes: Root cause: the server bound "http://localhost:{port}/", which only listens on loopback. Now it binds "http://+:{port}/" (all interfaces). task.name: drag glitchyness
task.prompt: dragging to re-order is very glitchy, the positions kind of mess up and its just overall not very smooth, lets have tasks gradually move out of the way rather than snap and make the whole thing a lot more pleasing
task.requirements: dragging is less glitchy and more appealing
task.notes: Two causes of the glitchiness in the row-reorder drag: (1) the insert-index maths read the mid-flight animated TranslateTransform value (`GetTranslateY(c) > 0`) to guess a row's rest position, so while rows were still animating the computed midpoints flickered and the gap jumped back and forth; (2) the dragged row was removed with an instant Visibility=Collapsed and rows below snapped up, and on drop every row had its transform cleared instantly. Fixes: track the intended offset per row in a `_targetOffset` dictionary and subtract THAT (never the live transform) when computing midpoints, so the insert index is stable; animate the source row's height+opacity to zero over 140ms (new CollapseRow/RestoreRow) instead of snapping; lengthen the move animation to 200ms with EaseInOut and always re-target so a change of direction is followed smoothly. VisibleContainers now excludes the dragged row explicitly. Build succeeds, 0 warnings.

task.name: dispatcher
task.prompt:
I was thinking about how to deal with adding/editing tasks while an agent is running and i came up with the idea for the "operator" a cli tool that facilitates everything. basically this app, the agents, and the webserver will interact with the operator. the operator can do the tasks below and will keep the program state accurate.
the operator runs a file called "queue" that stores a list of job (what project, what task, what job) and it pushes the queue as items arrive and then it removes them.
if you can think of any other skills the operator needs to keep this all in sync then goahead and add the ability.
calls to the operator should run in the background and NOT open a new window
task.requirements: operator in place with all subtasks working
task.notes:
Built the "operator" - the single choke-point through which the app, the AI agents and the web server mutate a project's tasks.xml, so writes never interleave while an agent is running.
CORE (new PromptQueue.Core/Operator/): OperatorEngine (queue + apply + save), OperatorJob (a queued change: command + string args + optional XML payload), OperatorResult, CrossProcessLock (system-wide named mutex "Global\zProject.Operator", abandoned-mutex tolerant), TaskFields (field-name -> TaskItem setter map with aliases). Every mutating call becomes a job appended to a persistent queue file at %LOCALAPPDATA%/PromptQueue/operator/queue.xml, then the whole queue is drained under the mutex; a job is removed only after it is applied and the affected project saved via ProjectStore.Save, so a crash mid-drain just retries. Read calls (read/list) skip the queue. ProjectStore.Save now also takes that same mutex around the tasks.xml write, so the app and the operator serialise against each other.
Commands: read <project>, list, sync <task_id> <field> <value>, new_task <project> <name> [prompt] (prints new id), new_subtask <task_id> <text>, delete <task_id>, move <task_id> <index>. Extra skills added to keep state in sync: list, subtask_done (toggle a subtask by index), upsert (full task replace/add - used by the app's task editor). <project> resolves by name, id-prefix or directory path; <task_id> is looked up across all registered projects.
EXE (new PromptQueue.Operator, AssemblyName zProject_operator): thin arg-parser over OperatorEngine. Console app, exits when done, never opens its own window (callers launch it hidden). Added to PromptQueue.slnx; built into builds/debug + builds/release next to zProject.exe.
APP (subtask 9 - "switched to interacting with the operator"): MainViewModel routes every task mutation through OperatorEngine in-process (same mutex + queue as the exe) via a new ApplyViaOperator helper that runs the op then re-reads the project from disk (carrying card-collapse state across the reload) so the UI shows exactly what was persisted. Re-routed: quick-add, Add/Edit task form (mint id via new_task then upsert), delete, drag-move, done toggle (row + card checkbox), lock toggle, subtask checkbox. Removed the now-dead AfterTasksChanged/SaveCurrent. Whole solution builds clean, 0 warnings; operator CLI round-trip verified (new_task/sync/new_subtask/move/delete, queue drains to empty).

task.notes: Infrastructure: new TaskItem.LockKey (string) serialized as a <lockKey> element by TaskXmlSerializer (write + read, trimmed), carried through Clone/CopyFrom, and added to every existing task in this file. task.prompt: right next to add task, add a text field for comma seperated tags, keep track (per project) of each tag and autocomplete exisiting ones as they are typed. color code each tag a random color, again this is for easy identification, these tags will also be saved to the xml (text only) so the agent cant tell what it is

Each /api/project/{i} call re-reads that project's tasks.xml, so switching projects always shows fresh data. The app's new "Server > Start Web View Server" menu launches zProject_server.exe (a console app, so it opens its own window). A build now means building BOTH projects into the same folder (documented in instructions.txt); zProject.exe, zProject_server.exe and zProject_webView.html are co-located in builds/test, builds/debug and builds/release. Verified end to end: picker + task view render correctly (headless screenshots), API returns all projects/tasks, console logs address/requests/connect/disconnect.
